description_good_justification: README.md opens with a clear one-line description: 'HMS is a high-performance vector memory engine for Node.js, powered by Rust via N-API. It implements Vector Symbolic Architectures (VSA) using Binary Spatter Code (BSC) to deliver semantic search, analogical reasoning, relational knowledge graphs, and associative memory at scale.'
interact_justification: README.md links Installation/Quick Start (obtain), and CONTRIBUTING.md + GitHub Issues (https://github.com/writerslogic/holographic-memory/issues) explain how to give feedback and contribute via PRs.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md describes the process: fork, branch, commit, push, open a PR, plus a 'Development Setup' section (rustup MSRV 1.82, npm install, npm run build, cargo test --workspace --lib).
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Style Guidelines' section specifies cargo fmt, 'cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings (zero warnings required)', JS 2-space/camelCase, and a required commit-message format ('<type>: <description>').
floss_license_justification: Apache License 2.0, an OSI-approved FLOSS license, confirmed in the LICENSE file and package.json/Cargo.toml ('license: Apache-2.0').
floss_license_osi_justification: Apache-2.0 is OSI-approved (https://opensource.org/licenses/Apache-2.0), as referenced in the README license badge.
license_location_justification: LICENSE file present at repo root (/Volumes/A/holographic-memory/LICENSE), full Apache-2.0 text, standard location.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md provides installation, quick start, features, architecture, and performance sections; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/INTEGRATION.md, docs/PRIVACY.md, docs/SECURITY.md provide further basic documentation.
documentation_interface_justification: index.d.ts documents the full TypeScript/N-API interface (inputs/outputs of the public API); docs.rs badge points to generated Rust API docs from doc comments in src/.
sites_https_justification: Repo is hosted at https://github.com/writerslogic/holographic-memory (HTTPS); homepage in package.json/Cargo.toml is https://writerslogic.com/holographic-memory and https://docs.rs/holographic-memory, both HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues (https://github.com/writerslogic/holographic-memory/issues) is used as a searchable, URL-addressable discussion mechanism open to any GitHub user; no proprietary client required. 26 open issues observed via `gh api repos/writerslogic/holographic-memory/issues`.
english_justification: All documentation (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, docs/*.md) and commit messages are in English.
maintained_justification: `git log` shows active commits through 2026-07-21 (most recent: 6b98b0f) with continuous history since first commit 2026-05-14, plus automated Dependabot PRs merged as recently as 2026-08-10 per `gh api .../pulls`. Project is under 4 months old and actively developed.
repo_public_justification: `gh api repos/writerslogic/holographic-memory` reports visibility: public; repo URL https://github.com/writerslogic/holographic-memory.
repo_track_justification: Git repository (`.git/`) tracks author, timestamp, and diff for every change; verified via `git log --format='%ad %an %s'` showing named authors (David Condrey, github-actions[bot], dependabot[bot]) and dates for every commit.
repo_interim_justification: `git log --oneline` shows many commits between tagged releases (e.g. dozens of commits between v0.5.0 and v0.6.0 tags), not just release commits.
repo_distributed_justification: Repository uses Git, a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml and package.json both declare version 0.6.0; git tags v0.4.0, v0.5.0, v0.6.0, py-v0.6.0 each map to a unique commit.
version_semver_justification: Versions follow SemVer (0.4.0, 0.5.0, 0.6.0) as declared in Cargo.toml/package.json.
version_tags_justification: `git tag` lists v0.4.0, v0.5.0, v0.6.0, py-v0.6.0, matching GitHub releases confirmed via `gh api repos/writerslogic/holographic-memory/releases`.
release_notes_justification: GitHub Releases have human-written notes, e.g. v0.6.0 'Provenance & Content Credentials' (1775 chars of prose, not a raw commit dump), confirmed via `gh api repos/writerslogic/holographic-memory/releases`. CHANGELOG.md is auto-generated from Conventional Commits (cliff.toml) and grouped by category (Added/Changed/Fixed/Documentation).
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed in any release to date (no CVEs or security advisories found via `gh api repos/writerslogic/holographic-memory/security-advisories` scope reviewed); N/A per criterion.
report_process_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Reporting Bugs' section directs users to the GitHub Issue Tracker; issues are open at https://github.com/writerslogic/holographic-memory/issues.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is used for individual issues; 59 issues/PRs observed via `gh api repos/writerslogic/holographic-memory/issues`, each tracked individually with number/state/labels.
report_responses_justification: No qualifying reports exist to assess a majority against (evidence: Reviewed all open/closed issues via `gh api repos/writerslogic/holographic-memory/issues?state=all`: the majority are Dependabot/automated PRs, all acknowledged and merged/closed (comments present, closed same-day-to-weeks). The remaining open non-PR issues (e.g. #39-#51) are maintainer-authored roadmap/feature-tracking issues, not external bug reports; no external bug report has been filed and left unacknowledged in the last 2-12 months.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
enhancement_responses_justification: No qualifying enhancement requests exist to assess a majority against (evidence: Same evidence as report_responses: the open roadmap-style issues (#1-#10, #39-#51) are self-filed maintainer planning issues, not external enhancement requests awaiting a response; no external enhancement request has been left unanswered in the tracker.). Marked unknown rather than asserting a vacuous Met.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provides a publicly available, searchable archive of all reports and responses at https://github.com/writerslogic/holographic-memory/issues (open and closed, e.g. #1-#59 all viewable).
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md (repo root) publishes the process: 'Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues... Open a private advisory via GitHub Security Advisories... or email admin@writerslogic.com.'
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md explains two private-report channels: GitHub Security Advisories (private advisory link) and direct email to admin@writerslogic.com.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months (no entries found in `gh api repos/writerslogic/holographic-memory/security-advisories` or issue tracker); N/A per criterion since no reports exist to measure response time against.
build_justification: Automated build via Cargo (cargo build) for the Rust crate and `napi build --release --features node-api` (package.json 'scripts.build') for the Node native module, both exercised in .github/workflows/ci.yml ('build-napi' job).
build_common_tools_justification: Uses Cargo (standard Rust build tool) and npm/@napi-rs/cli (standard Node.js native-module tooling), both common FLOSS tools for these languages.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, npm, and @napi-rs/cli (devDependency in package.json) are all FLOSS; no proprietary build tool is required per Cargo.toml/package.json.
test_justification: 409 `#[test]` functions across 70 files with `#[cfg(test)]` modules in src/, plus src/lib_proptest.rs (property-based tests via proptest). CONTRIBUTING.md documents how to run them: 'Run tests: cargo test --workspace --lib'. Tests are FLOSS (built into cargo, Apache-2.0 licensed proptest crate).
test_invocation_justification: Tests are invoked with the standard Rust convention `cargo test`, as documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and used in .github/workflows/ci.yml ('Run Tests: cargo test --verbose').
test_most_justification: .github/workflows/coverage.yml runs `cargo llvm-cov --lib` on every push to main and publishes a coverage badge (README.md badge references .github/badges/coverage.json), showing coverage is measured; 409 test functions exercise core VSA operations, persistence, security, and graph modules.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --verbose` on every push and pull_request to main.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Development Setup' instructs contributors to run tests before submitting, and CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) gates every PR on `cargo test --verbose` passing; project convention (visible in commit history, e.g. multiple 'test:' commits) is to add tests with new functionality.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent commit history shows tests added alongside functional changes, e.g. src/lib_proptest.rs and 70 files with #[cfg(test)] modules covering core.entangled, security, provenance, nsg::graph; `git log` shows dedicated 'test:' commits accompanying feature work.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents how to run tests but does not explicitly state a policy that new functionality must include tests; no explicit contribution requirement to that effect found in CONTRIBUTING.md.
warnings_justification: Clippy (Rust's standard FLOSS linter) is enabled: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, and CONTRIBUTING.md requires 'cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings (zero warnings required)'.
warnings_fixed_justification: `-D warnings` in both CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and the documented contributor workflow (CONTRIBUTING.md) turns all clippy warnings into build failures, so warnings must be fixed before merge.
warnings_strict_justification: CI runs clippy with `--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, the strictest practical clippy invocation (all targets, all features, warnings as errors), plus `cargo fmt -- --check`.
know_secure_design_justification: docs/SECURITY.md contains an explicit threat model (Assets Protected, Threat Categories table with mitigations, Trust Boundaries) demonstrating secure-design knowledge, e.g. mapping 'Unauthorized read of stored data' to AES-256-GCM and 'Tampering with arena log' to CRC32/Ed25519 signatures.
know_common_errors_justification: docs/SECURITY.md 'Limitations' section explicitly discusses common vulnerability classes and their mitigations for this software: no key rotation, no access control, passphrase handling responsibility, CRC32 non-cryptographic caveat, no forward secrecy, salt-reuse tradeoff — showing awareness of common crypto/storage error classes.
crypto_published_justification: src/core/security.rs and docs/SECURITY.md show only publicly published, standard algorithms used: Ed25519 (ed25519-dalek), AES-256-GCM (aes-gcm), Argon2id (argon2), SHA-256 (sha2) — no proprietary or homegrown crypto.
crypto_call_justification: Cargo.toml dependencies show HMS calls established crypto crates (ed25519-dalek, aes-gcm, argon2, sha2) rather than reimplementing primitives itself, confirmed by `use argon2::Argon2` and aes_gcm::Aes256Gcm usage in src/core/security.rs.
crypto_floss_justification: All crypto dependencies (ed25519-dalek, aes-gcm, argon2, sha2) are FLOSS Rust crates (MIT/Apache-2.0 per deny.toml allow-list), so the crypto functionality is fully FLOSS-implementable.
crypto_keylength_justification: AES-256-GCM (256-bit keys) and Ed25519 (128-bit security level, standard NIST/IETF-recommended curve) are used per src/core/security.rs; both exceed NIST minimums through 2030.
crypto_working_justification: docs/SECURITY.md and src/core/security.rs confirm defaults use AES-256-GCM, Ed25519, Argon2id, and SHA-256 — none of the broken algorithms (MD4/MD5/single-DES/RC4/Dual_EC_DRBG) or bad cipher modes are used by default.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No SHA-1 or CBC-mode usage found; docs/SECURITY.md documents SHA-256 for ID hashing and AES-256-GCM (AEAD, not CBC) for encryption, avoiding algorithms with known serious weaknesses.
crypto_pfs_justification: HMS is a local, on-disk storage engine with no network key-agreement protocol; docs/SECURITY.md scope is local encryption-at-rest and audit-log signing, not a network transport, so perfect forward secrecy does not apply.
crypto_password_storage_justification: src/core/security.rs derives the encryption key via 'Argon2::default().hash_password_into(passphrase.as_bytes(), &salt, &mut key)' with a persisted 16-byte random salt (docs/SECURITY.md: 'Key derivation: Argon2id (default parameters) from user passphrase + 16-byte random salt'), matching the required iterated-hash-plus-salt scheme.
crypto_random_justification: src/core/security.rs uses `rand::rng().fill_bytes(&mut nonce_bytes)` for the AES-GCM nonce and `rand::thread_rng()` for Ed25519 key generation (docs/SECURITY.md: 'Key generation: rand::thread_rng() (OS CSPRNG via getrandom)'), both OS-backed CSPRNGs.
delivery_mitm_justification: Packages are delivered via npm (https://registry.npmjs.org, HTTPS) and crates.io (HTTPS), both enforced in .github/workflows/publish.yml and publish-crate.yml; git clone via GitHub uses HTTPS or SSH.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash-only integrity check over plain HTTP is used; npm publish uses `--provenance` with build attestations (.github/workflows/publish.yml 'Generate Generic Attestations' via actions/attest) and crates.io/npm both serve over HTTPS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Dependabot (.github/dependabot.yml, weekly cadence) and cargo-deny (deny.toml, run in CI via EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action) actively track advisories; recent PRs (#33-#38, merged within days per `gh api .../pulls`) show prompt dependency/security updates; no medium+ advisory found unaddressed beyond 60 days in deny.toml's tracked ignore list (each entry justified as no-safe-upgrade-path, not neglect).
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: PR #38 'security: remediate repository alerts and dependencies' and #53 'fix: resolve workflow code scanning alerts' were opened and closed within the same day (2026-08-06 to 2026-08-08 per `gh api .../issues`), showing rapid turnaround on flagged security issues.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Searched tracked source (src/, bindings/) for private-key headers and hardcoded API-key patterns via grep; none found. .gitignore excludes typical secret files. No .env files are tracked in the repo.
static_analysis_justification: Clippy (Rust's standard static analyzer) runs in .github/workflows/ci.yml on every push/PR ('cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings'); OpenSSF Scorecard (.github/workflows/scorecard.yml) also performs static supply-chain analysis.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: cargo-deny (deny.toml, run via .github/workflows/ci.yml 'deny' job and dependency-review.yml) checks advisories/bans/licenses/sources against the RustSec Advisory Database, which includes common-vulnerability rules for dependencies; GitHub CodeQL SARIF upload is wired via .github/workflows/scorecard.yml.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CI fails the build on any clippy warning (`-D warnings`) and cargo-deny failures block merges; commit de27497 'ci: add OpenSSF Scorecard, Dependency Review, and SECURITY.md (+ CodeQL/Dependabot where missing)' and PR #53 'fix: resolve workflow code scanning alerts' show findings are actively fixed.
static_analysis_often_justification: Clippy and cargo-deny run on every push and pull_request to main (.github/workflows/ci.yml), i.e. on every commit, exceeding the 'daily' threshold.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis tool (e.g. fuzzing via cargo-fuzz/AFL, or sanitizers) found in .github/workflows/ or Cargo.toml dev-dependencies; only static analysis (clippy, cargo-deny) and unit/property tests are present.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: `grep -rn unsafe src/ --include=*.rs` finds 9 occurrences of `unsafe` code in src/lib.rs and src/core/storage.rs, so memory-unsafe code is present, but no dynamic memory-safety tool (ASan, Miri, Valgrind) is configured anywhere in .github/workflows/.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic-analysis configuration exists in the repo (see dynamic_analysis, Unmet), so no assertion-enabling config for such a tool is present either.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis tool is currently run (see dynamic_analysis, Unmet), so there are no dynamic-analysis findings to fix.
